answer: analysis.py is complete and validated. It implements a stored-in-O(H*S*A) two-sequence optimistic Q-learner: (Q1) a one-step bootstrapped optimistic Q (visit-dependent mean of r+max_a Q1[h+1,next,a]) that keeps genuine optimism and max-structure, plus (Q2) a bounded W=10 delayed-credit return sequence rolled back at each episode boundary from the single bounded trace (visit-dependent mean + Welford centered moments, drift-free by construction). Selection blends index = KAPPA*(Q1+b1)+(1-KAPPA)*(Q2+b2), where b1/b2 are variance-sensitive bonuses whose variance term uses the *grounded* Q2 centered moments (not the drifting bootstrap variance) — this is the mechanism that removes the UCB-B burn-in cost — plus a count-based term and an experience-decay schedule (TAU=3000, floor 0.25) that keeps exploration early and shrinks it as the budget depletes. One shared config, no case branching. Official public runner: total regret 76.55 (beats strong-reference 77.57 and plain UCB-B 207.99); per-case noisy_fork 10.08, variance_cascade 3.41, stable_volatile 12.02, 0 invalid actions. Synthetic stress families (delayed-credit chains, noisy forks, volatile variance, tight many-action gaps): 36% lower expected policy regret than a plain UCB-B reference (1453 vs 2272 on a 6-construction x 3-eval battery). All constraints verified: no P/R needed, storage exactly 7 arrays x (H+1)*S*A plus trace<=H, no H*S*A*S tensor, no next-state counts, no replay/planning/posterior, stored Q within [0,remaining], deterministic, ~0.8 s full-suite runtime.
